text: hey everybody I am frequently asked about the King James version as a translation and I generally don't recommend it it is most valuable as an
artifact of the English language but as a translation is based on inferior manuscripts its translation philosophy
is far too literal and awkward and it is phenomenally outdated and so it is very difficult to understand and folks who
believe that they understand it well enough don't unless they have extensively studied it's translation
philosophy The Source text the Hebrew the Greek and don't need to ask me if it's a good translation or not and I'll give one example of how it can be
misleading the book of Jude only has one chapter verse 22 it says but of some have compassion making a difference and
most people today almost everybody would interpret this to mean when we have compassion on people we can have a positive influence or impact on their
lives we can make a difference for them and that's a wonderful message and it has absolutely nothing to do with what the King James translators were trying
to say because that phrase making a difference didn't come to refer to having a positive influence or impact on
someone until around the year 1900 for multiple centuries it did not mean that
it meant make a distinction exercise discernment so when the King James translators rendered this passage what
they meant was have compassion on some but be Discerning on whom and even that has absolutely nothing to
do with the message that the author of The Epistle of Jude was trying to communicate because the King James version is based on inferior manuscripts
the participle that is translated making a difference occurs in the manuscripts used by the King James translators in
the nominative case meaning it is connected with the subject of the Clause we now know because we have many more reliable and many more ancient
manuscripts that that participle should be in the accusative case it should be the object of the verb and so most
translations today will render something more like have compassion on those who are doubting or wavering so that make a
distinction exercise discernment you're having compassion on those who are trying to make a distinction trying to discern and so that is generally
interpreted either as people who are wavering people who are doubting or people who are outside of the Church community so it's actually an entirely
different message Al together and if we rely on the King James version we would not understand that there are much better Bible translations out there I
highly recommend the new revised Standard Version updated Edition those who are looking for a translation of both the Hebrew Bible and the New Testament and there will be a sixth
edition of the New Oxford annotated Bible that will be coming out probably next year so I would keep an eye out for that
